definitions: To intentionally make something dark by turning off lights or covering windows.
To censor or obscure information in a document or broadcast.
To experience a temporary loss of memory, often due to alcohol or drugs.
examples: She tends to black out when she sees blood.
The city decided to black out the lights during the air raid.
Parts of the report were blacked out for national security.
He couldn't remember the party; he must have blacked out.
